claims.text: High-entropy alloys typically exist as disordered solid solutions containing multiple principal elements.

A framework combining machine learning with physics-based descriptors of local chemical disorder and atomic vibrational spectra will predict low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than existing methods.
Local atomic-scale chemical disorder affects phonon scattering.
Capturing local disorder will improve the model's representation of phonon dispersion.
Capturing local disorder will improve the model's representation of phonon scattering.
Improved representation of phonon dispersion and scattering will allow the model to resolve the dominant heat-blocking mechanisms.
Resolving the dominant heat-blocking mechanisms will improve predictions of phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will predict phonon thermal conductivity to within approximately 20% of experimental measurements.
Current models typically deviate from experimental phonon thermal conductivity by approximately 40% or more.
Current predictive models generally neglect detailed local-disorder effects.
The predicted improvement applies primarily to alloys with high chemical disorder and no significant long-range ordering.
The predicted improvement may not extend to materials containing significant ordered micro-domains.
The predicted improvement may not extend to extreme temperatures where additional phonon-scattering mechanisms become dominant.
Model performance can be benchmarked by comparing predicted and measured phonon thermal conductivities across high-entropy alloys with varying chemical disorder.
Failure to achieve approximately 20% prediction error, or failure to improve statistically significantly over existing models, will falsify the hypothesis.
